---
title: "The Dominican Sinker Tradition"
format: html
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

Across Latin America, and particularly in the Dominican Republic, pitching culture has long prioritized arm-side run, heavy sinking life, and inducing ground balls. Rather than altering natural mechanics to chase high four-seam backspin, Dominican player development and academies frequently hone natural three-quarter arm slots that let fastballs run aggressively toward the arm side.

This lineage was immortalized by Hall of Famer Pedro Martínez—whose devastating two-seamer and changeup rode on explosive arm-side movement—and Bartolo Colón, who built a legendary two-decade career leaning on unhittable two-seam tail. That philosophy thrives today in Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara and Red Sox starter Brayan Bello (who trained directly under Pedro Martínez). Dominican sinkers in this dataset average 96.0 mph with over 16 inches of tailing run, allowing pitchers to attack early in the count and generate weak contact.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

# Load Statcast pitching data
pitch_data <- read_csv("data/statcast_pitchers.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Map Statcast pitch abbreviations to full names
pitch_labels <- c(
  "FF" = "4-Seam Fastball",
  "SI" = "Sinker",
  "SL" = "Slider",
  "CH" = "Changeup",
  "FC" = "Cutter",
  "ST" = "Sweeper",
  "CU" = "Curveball",
  "FS" = "Splitter",
  "KC" = "Knuckle Curve",
  "SV" = "Slurve"
)

# Identify the top 6 countries by pitch volume
top_countries <- pitch_data |>
  count(country_name) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 6) |>
  pull(country_name)

clean_data <- pitch_data |>
  filter(country_name %in% top_countries, pitch_type %in% names(pitch_labels))

# Calculate sinker usage percentage across top countries
sinker_rates <- clean_data |>
  group_by(country_name) |>
  summarize(
    total = n(),
    sinkers = sum(pitch_type == "SI"),
    pct = round(sinkers / total * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    is_dr = ifelse(country_name == "Dominican Republic", "Dominican Republic", "Other Countries")
  )

# Bar chart comparing sinker usage across countries
p_sinker <- ggplot(sinker_rates, aes(
  x = pct,
  y = reorder(country_name, pct),
  fill = is_dr,
  text = paste0(
    "<b>", country_name, "</b><br>",
    "Sinker Usage: ", pct, "%<br>",
    "Sinkers: ", scales::comma(sinkers), " / ", scales::comma(total)
  )
)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Dominican Republic" = "#002D62", "Other Countries" = "#8da0cb")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, 35)) +
  labs(
    title = "Sinker Reliance by Pitcher Nationality",
    subtitle = "Dominican pitchers throw sinkers at 28.5%—well above other nations",
    x = "Usage (%)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggplotly(p_sinker, tooltip = "text")
```
